cards.task: Pick up the key, then reach the goal.

wrong.why: Takes the key and opens the door, then waits and never reaches the goal.
Never takes the key and never reaches the goal.

paraphrases: Take the key and then get to the goal.
Grab the key first, then make your way to the goal.
After you have picked up the key, reach the goal.
cards.notes: The other clause is implied by the finish, so the env reward pays exactly when it is done.

cards.task: Flip the switch on the wall.

wrong.why: Ignores the siren and never touches the switch.

paraphrases: Toggle the wall switch.
Operate the switch fixed to the wall.
At some point, flip the wall switch.

cards.task: Open the door and pick up the box in the other room.

wrong.why: Takes the key and opens the door, then waits and never picks up the box.

cards.task: Pick up the ball that blocks the door.

wrong.why: Does nothing, so the ball stays in front of the door.

cards.task: Get into the locked room and pick up the ball.

wrong.why: Takes the key and opens the locked door, then waits outside the room.

cards.task: Open the door.

wrong.why: Does nothing, so the door stays locked.

cards.task: Be holding the key on at least two different moves, then pick up the box in the other room.

wrong.why: Holds the key and opens the door, then waits and never picks up the box.

paraphrases: First have the key in your hands on at least two separate moves; afterwards pick up the box in the other room.
Pick up the box in the other room, after you were holding the key on at least two different moves.
Hold the key on two or more different moves, and then take the box from the other room.
cards.notes: State reading: the judge counts two different steps with the state true (not necessarily consecutive). The other clause is implied by the finish, so the env reward pays exactly when it is done. Any successful box pickup holds the key on two or more steps, so the counting clause cannot be isolated on this goal card; the nogoal sibling tests it.

cards.task: Be holding the key on at least two different moves.

wrong.why: Never takes the key.
Picks up the key and stops there, so it is held on one step only.

paraphrases: Hold the key on two or more different moves.
Carry the key on at least two different moves.
Have the key in your hands on at least two separate moves.
cards.notes: Changed in card fix 2: added the once-against-twice negative (the plan ends at the first pickup), which this trained counting card lacked.

cards.task: Be holding the key on at least two different moves, then pick up the box in the other room.

wrong.why: Clears the ball and takes the key, opens the door, then waits and never picks up the box.

cards.task: Be holding the matching key on at least two different moves.

wrong.why: Picks up the key and stops there, so it is held on one step only.

cards.notes: Changed in card fix 2: the once-against-twice negative now ends at the first pickup; the earlier drop step could walk and turn first, so on KeyCorridor seeds 14, 15 and 20 the key stayed in hand for several steps and the plan passed.

cards.task: Be holding the key on at least two different moves, open the door and reach the goal.

wrong.why: Holds the key and opens the door, then waits and never reaches the goal.

cards.task: Be holding the key on at least two different moves.

wrong.why: Picks up the key and stops there, so it is held on one step only.

cards.notes: Changed in card fix 2: the once-against-twice negative now ends at the first pickup; the earlier drop step could walk and turn first, so on UnlockPickup seeds 4, 8, 26 and 36 the key stayed in hand for several steps and the plan passed.

cards.task: Pick up the box in the other room, and never drop the key while the door is still closed.

wrong.why: Takes the key before the ball and has to drop it with the door closed, then finishes.
Moves the ball, takes the key and opens the door, then waits and never picks up the box.

paraphrases: Never drop the key while the door is still closed, and pick up the box in the other room.
Get the box from the other room, and do not drop the key while the door is closed.
While the door is still closed, you must not drop the key. Pick up the box in the other room.
cards.notes: With the finish, Absence(key_lost) and NotCoExistence(key_lost, door_open) mean the same.

cards.task: Never open the locked door.

wrong.why: Takes the key and opens the locked door.

paraphrases: Do not open the locked door.
Keep the locked door shut.
The locked door must never be opened.

cards.task: Reach the goal, and never drop the key while the door is still closed.

wrong.why: Drops the key while the door is still closed, picks it up again, then finishes.
Keeps the key and opens the door, then waits and never reaches the goal.

cards.task: Don't drop the key while the door is still closed.

wrong.why: Takes the key first and drops it again to free its hands for the ball.

cards.task: Pick up the box in the other room, and never drop the key while the door is still closed.

wrong.why: Drops the key with the door closed, picks it up again, then finishes.
Keeps the key and opens the door, then waits and never picks up the box.

cards.task: Never flip the wall switch.

wrong.why: Turns the siren off with the switch.

cards.notes: The siren rings, so the solving plan has to leave it ringing. Changed in card fix 2: the wording is one action, flipping the switch (the clause observes toggling only), not touching or bumping its panel.

cards.task: Once you have found the key, the locked door must be open on the last step of the episode. Open it, then pick up the ball.

wrong.why: Takes the key, then waits: the locked door is never opened.
Takes the key and opens the locked door, then waits and never picks up the ball.

paraphrases: After you find the key, make sure the locked door is open when the episode ends. Open it and then take the ball.
From the moment you find the key, the locked door has to be open on the final step. Open it, and then pick up the ball.
When you find the key, the locked door must be open at the end of the episode; open it. Finally, pick up the ball.
cards.notes: The response is the door, checked on the last step (the key is dropped later). Changed in card fix 2: the trigger key_found stays true once set, so Response needs the door open on the final step of the trace, not all the way through. The task says exactly that and not 'keep it open': a run that shuts the door and opens it again satisfies the clause. `key_found` also needs a clear view of the key now.

cards.task: Whenever the ball is out of the way of the door, you must be holding the key at that moment or pick it up afterwards.

wrong.why: Moves the ball, then waits and never takes the key.

paraphrases: At every moment the ball is out of the way of the door, you have to be carrying the key then, or pick it up later.
If the ball has been moved away from the door, you must be holding the key at that point or at some later point.
Any time the ball is away from the door, the key must be in your hands at that moment or afterwards.
cards.notes: Changed in card fix 2: the trigger blocker_moved is a condition, not a latch (false again when the ball is dropped back on its cell), so Response needs the key in hand at the last moment the ball was out of the way or later. The task says exactly that and not 'keep holding it': a run that puts the key down and takes it again, or restores the ball and then takes and drops the key, satisfies the clause.

cards.task: Whenever you are holding the key, the door must be open at that moment or opened afterwards. Then reach the goal.

wrong.why: Takes the key, then waits: the door is never opened.
Takes the key and opens the door, then waits and never reaches the goal.

cards.notes: No also_ok: Response and Precedence on a state that can turn false again are not equivalent. Changed in card fix 2: the trigger has_key stays true while the key is held, so the door must be open when the key was last held or later; the task now states that condition instead of the event reading, and a trace that opens then shuts the door while still holding the key fails by that wording.

cards.task: Whenever you are holding the key, the door must be open at that moment or opened afterwards.

wrong.why: Takes the key, then waits: the door is never opened.

cards.notes: Changed in card fix 2: the trigger has_door_key stays true while the key is held, so the door must be open when the key was last held or later; the task now states that condition instead of the event reading, and a trace that opens then shuts the door while still holding the key fails by that wording.

cards.task: Whenever you are holding the key, the door must be open at that moment or opened afterwards. Then pick up the box in the other room.

wrong.why: Clears the ball and takes the key, then waits: the door is never opened.

cards.notes: Changed in card fix 2: the trigger has_door_key stays true while the key is held, so the door must be open when the key was last held or later; the task now states that condition instead of the event reading, and a trace that opens then shuts the door while still holding the key fails by that wording.

cards.task: Once you have found the key, the locked door must be open on the last step of the episode.

wrong.why: Takes the key, then waits: the locked door is never opened.

cards.notes: Changed in card fix 2: the trigger key_found stays true once set, so Response needs the door open on the final step of the trace, not all the way through. The task says exactly that and not 'leave it open': a run that shuts the door and opens it again satisfies the clause.

cards.task: Move the ball away from the door before you take the key, then open the door and pick up the box.

wrong.why: Takes the key before the ball is moved, then fixes it and finishes.
Does it in the right order but waits after opening the door.

paraphrases: Before taking the key, move the ball away from the door. Then open the door and pick up the box.
Take the key only after the ball is out of the way, then open the door and pick up the box.
First move the ball off the door, then take the key, open the door and pick up the box.
cards.notes: Not forced by the env: the key can be taken first (it is then dropped to free the hands).

cards.task: If you reach the exit, you must have flipped the switch first.

wrong.why: Ignores the siren, so the exit is reached with no switch toggled before.

paraphrases: You may only reach the exit after you have flipped the switch.
Do not reach the exit until you have flipped the switch.
Reaching the exit is allowed only once the switch has been flipped.
cards.notes: The first ring comes at step 1-4 and the exit is at least 6 moves away, so the policy toggles first. Changed in card fix 2: one conditional reading in every wording (a run that never flips the switch and never reaches the exit also passes); the earlier imperative could be read as asking for both.

cards.task: Do not drop the key while the door is closed until the door has been opened once. Reach the goal.

wrong.why: Drops the key while the door is still closed, picks it up again, then finishes.

cards.task: Don't drop the key while the door is closed until the door has been opened once.

wrong.why: Drops the key at once, with the door still closed.

cards.task: Pick up the box in the other room, but do not drop the key while the door is closed until the door has been opened once.

wrong.why: Drops the key while the door is still closed, picks it up again, then finishes.

cards.task: Do not take the key until you have moved the ball away from the door.

wrong.why: Takes the key before the ball is moved.

cards.notes: Changed in card fix 2: the wording is the conditional ban (taking the key is allowed only after the ball has moved); a run that moves nothing and takes nothing also passes, so the earlier imperative no longer reads as a required action.

cards.task: Carry the box to the exit. Whenever the box falls, pick it up again on your very next move.

wrong.why: Does not react to the fall and reaches the exit without the box.
Walks straight to the exit and never touches the box.

paraphrases: Take the box to the exit. Each time the box falls, pick it up on your very next move.
Reach the exit with the box in your hands, and if the box falls, pick it up again on the very next move.
Get to the exit carrying the box; every time the box falls, your very next move must pick it up again.
cards.notes: Event room only: box_fell is an event, so the judge table can hold. The next-step pickup works when the box lands on the free front cell (the first cell tried); the solving policy waits in place with the box until its falls are done. The env require holding_box is deliberate: a fall only starts after a pickup. Changed in card fix 2: the task asks to carry the box to the exit, checked at the exit step (Response(at_exit, holding_box)), so a direct exit no longer passes; the solving policy was fixed for wall-side falls.

cards.task: Whenever the box falls, pick it up again on your very next move. If you reach the exit, you must be carrying the box.

wrong.why: Does not react to the fall and reaches the exit without the box.
Walks straight to the exit and never touches the box.

paraphrases: Should the box fall, make your very next move the one that picks it back up. If you get to the exit, you must have the box in your hands.
Every time the box falls, your very next move must pick it up again; and if you reach the exit, you must be carrying the box.
After the box falls, the move right after it has to pick it up again. Do not reach the exit without the box in your hands.
cards.notes: Changed in card fix 2: the exit is not required, but a run that reaches it must carry the box at that step (Response(at_exit, holding_box)), so a direct exit no longer passes; the solving policy was fixed for wall-side falls. Staying put still satisfies both clauses.

cards.task: Carry the box to the exit. Each time the box falls, your very next move must pick it up again.

wrong.why: Does not react to the fall and reaches the exit without the box.
Walks straight to the exit and never touches the box.

cards.notes: The siren rings too; the task ignores it on purpose (distractor), and the solving policy ignores it. The env require holding_box is deliberate: a fall only starts after a pickup. Changed in card fix 2: the task asks to carry the box to the exit, checked at the exit step (Response(at_exit, holding_box)), so a direct exit no longer passes; the solving policy was fixed for wall-side falls and the siren detour.

cards.task: Each time the box falls, pick it up again on your very next move. If you reach the exit, you must be carrying the box.

wrong.why: Does not react to the fall and reaches the exit without the box.
Walks straight to the exit and never touches the box.

cards.notes: The siren rings too; the task ignores it on purpose (distractor), and the solving policy ignores it. Changed in card fix 2: the exit is not required, but a run that reaches it must carry the box at that step (Response(at_exit, holding_box)), so a direct exit no longer passes; the solving policy was fixed for wall-side falls and the siren detour. Staying put still satisfies both clauses.

cards.task: Carry the box to the exit. If the box falls, pick it up again on your very next move.

wrong.why: Does not react to the fall and reaches the exit without the box.
Walks straight to the exit and never touches the box.

cards.notes: The env require holding_box is deliberate: a fall only starts after a pickup. Changed in card fix 2: the task asks to carry the box to the exit, checked at the exit step (Response(at_exit, holding_box)), so a direct exit no longer passes; the solving policy was fixed for wall-side falls.

cards.task: If the box falls, the very next move must pick it up again. If you reach the exit, you must be carrying the box.

wrong.why: Does not react to the fall and reaches the exit without the box.
Walks straight to the exit and never touches the box.

cards.notes: Changed in card fix 2: the exit is not required, but a run that reaches it must carry the box at that step (Response(at_exit, holding_box)), so a direct exit no longer passes; the solving policy was fixed for wall-side falls. Staying put still satisfies both clauses.

cards.task: If you find the key, you must also open the locked door. Then pick up the ball.

wrong.why: Takes the key, then waits: the locked door is never opened.
Takes the key and opens the locked door, then waits and never picks up the ball.

paraphrases: Should you find the key, you are also required to open the locked door. After that, get the ball.
Finding the key means you must open the locked door too; finally, pick up the ball.
Pick up the ball. If you find the key, you need to open the locked door as well.
cards.notes: Order is free. The other clause is implied by the finish, so the env reward pays exactly when it is done. Changed in card fix 2: `key_found` needs a clear view of the key (no credit through a wall); the task text is unchanged.

cards.task: If you pick up the key, you must also open the door.

wrong.why: Takes the key, then waits: the door is never opened.

paraphrases: If you take the key, you also have to open the door.
Taking the key means you must open the door too.
You must open the door if you pick up the key.

cards.task: If you move the ball, you must also take the key. Then pick up the box in the other room.

wrong.why: Moves the ball, then waits: the key is never taken.
Moves the ball and takes the key, then waits and never picks up the box.

cards.task: If the siren rings at any point in the run, you must flip the switch at least once somewhere in the run, before or after the ring.

wrong.why: Ignores the siren, so the switch is never toggled.

cards.notes: Changed in card fix 2: the wording says one toggle anywhere in the run is enough when the siren rings, not one toggle after every ring (that is Response).

cards.task: If you take the key, you must also open the door. Then pick up the box in the other room.

wrong.why: Takes the key, then waits: the door is never opened.

cards.task: If you pick up the key, you must also open the door.

wrong.why: Takes the key, then waits: the door is never opened.

cards.task: Pick up the box in the other room, but never both drop the key while the door is still closed and open the door.

wrong.why: Takes the key before the ball, drops it with the door closed, then finishes.
Moves the ball, takes the key and opens the door, then waits and never picks up the box.

paraphrases: Get the box from the other room, while never letting both of these happen: you drop the key while the door is still closed, you open the door.
Pick up the box in the other room. You must not drop the key while the door is still closed and open the door in the same run.
Take the box from the other room; dropping the key while the door is still closed and opening the door must never both happen.

cards.task: Never both take the key and move the ball away from the door.

wrong.why: Moves the ball and then takes the key, so both happen.

paraphrases: Taking the key and moving the ball away from the door must never both happen.
Do not both pick up the key and move the ball away from the door.
Make sure you never do both: pick up the key and clear the ball from the door.
cards.notes: The key can be reached without moving the ball. Doing neither also satisfies the clause.

cards.task: Pick up the box in the other room, but never both drop the key while the door is still closed and open the door.

wrong.why: Drops the key, picks it up again, then opens the door and finishes.

cards.task: Never both drop the key while the door is still closed and open the door.

wrong.why: Drops the key, picks it up again, then opens the door.

cards.task: Reach the goal, but never both drop the key while the door is still closed and open the door.

wrong.why: Drops the key, picks it up again, then opens the door and finishes.
Takes the key and opens the door, then waits and never reaches the goal.

cards.task: Never both take the matching key and get into the locked room.

wrong.why: Takes the key, opens the locked door and goes in.

cards.notes: Entering the room needs the key, so the only way to obey is to stay out.
